olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Find all 4-digit positive integers with all digits perfect squares, divisible by $2,3,5,7$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2016

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Acute $\triangle ABC$ with circumcircle $\Gamma$, $M$ = midpoint of $BC$. $N$ on arc $BC$ (not containing $A$) with $\angle NAC=\angle BAM$. $R,S$ = midpoints of $AM,AN$; $T$ = foot of altitude from $A$. Prove $R,S,T$ are collinear.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2016

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $Q(x)=x^3-21x+35$ has three real roots. Find $a,b$ such that $P(x)=x^2+ax+b$ cyclically permutes the roots: if $r,s,t$ are roots of $Q$ then $P(r)=s,P(s)=t,P(t)=r$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2016

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Board starts with 3. Players alternate (Ana first): replace $n$ with an integer $m$ coprime to $n$ with $n<m<n^2$. First to reach $\geq 2016$ loses. Who wins?
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2016

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Call $\frac{1}{1+\frac{1}{k}}$ \textit{irie} for positive integer $k$. Prove every $n\geq 2$ can be written as a product of $r$ distinct irie numbers for every integer $r\geq n-1$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2016

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $\triangle ABC$ with incenter $I$, circumcircle $\Gamma$; $M=BI\cap\Gamma$, $N=CI\cap\Gamma$. Line through $I$ parallel to $MN$ meets $AB,AC$ at $P,Q$. Prove the circumradii of $\triangle BNP$ and $\triangle CMQ$ are equal.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2016
